facts.fact: Minutes of the project's consultations with councils, annexed to the plan, record a M'mbelwa district executive member on 11 July 2024 speaking of the internet the Digital Malawi Project provided to the councils as very slow and unreliable, which the project team accepted, and a regional meeting of June 2024 recording that Kasungu has 5MB on the Boma network, that the project bought Wi-Fi adapters so council desktops could receive the Wi-Fi 6 provided, and that the Department of E-Government can raise a council's bandwidth on request.
facts.system: Boma network / Government Wide Area Network (GWAN)

facts.fact: The consultation minutes of June and July 2024 record council officers logging in to the Boma network internet with passwords and meeting a 50MB limit on file attachments, some sites requiring a government email or ID to reach the internet, and councils still waiting for government email accounts: Dedza District Council was promised them by 1 July 2024 and Lilongwe City Council had supplied staff details long before with nothing done.
facts.system: Boma network / Government Wide Area Network (GWAN)

facts.fact: The consultation minutes of June and July 2024 speak of internet provided to the councils by the Digital Malawi Project and name Kasungu as on the Boma network, record on 25 June 2024 that Dowa was yet to be connected under that project and that some sites from it were not working, and give no count of councils connected against the 35 district, municipal and city councils the plan says exist.
facts.system: Boma network / Government Wide Area Network (GWAN)

facts.fact: The consultation minutes of June and July 2024 say the Department of E-Government manages the councils' internet on the government network, setting each institution's bandwidth and attachment limits and issuing government email, and that it is short of technical staff to support all 35 local councils promptly.
facts.system: Boma network / Government Wide Area Network (GWAN)

facts.fact: The consultation minutes of June and July 2024 say the councils' internet was provided by the Digital Malawi Project and that its successor has a ten-year agreement with contractors to provide and maintain the service, with the government to take it into its budget through E-Government once World Bank funding ends; a council participant said on 25 June 2024 that council ICT offices get no funding to buy data bundles or small equipment.
facts.system: Boma network / Government Wide Area Network (GWAN)

systems.system: Boma network / Government Wide Area Network (GWAN)
systems.platform: Wi-Fi 6 at sites; optic fibre, wireless and satellite named for the successor project
systems.owner: Department of E-Government, Ministry of Information and Digitalization; provided under the Digital Malawi (Foundations) Project run by the Public Private Partnership Commission
systems.tiers: district, municipal and city councils among the government institutions connected; Kasungu named at 5MB, Dowa not yet connected in June 2024
national platform to link with the National Registration Bureau, Immigration and banks; councils invited to use it for property rates and e-ticketing, not yet on it in June 2024
to hold data for ministries, departments and agencies, councils' included; no council to have its own

systems.owner: the Digital Malawi project with the FINES project
systems.tiers: national, for revenue collection; in development in June 2024

note: Passages only. The facts come from meeting minutes: what council officers and the project team said in June and July 2024, not a survey. The Digital Malawi Acceleration Project itself, which is to connect more government offices with councils choosing the sites, is preparation and gives no fact.
